purpose: Resolve the native waiting resource before choosing one mitigation.
comparisons: Kernel native sync intervals nested under file_write_and_wait_range, jbd2_log_wait_commit, and blkdev_issue_flush; report their union and unattributed remainder.
Ext4 device/inode and jbd2 transaction identities for journal and checkpoint calls.
Existing application trace retains first receipt waits, queues, checkpoints and exact request sequences independently of kernel clock.

Only join kernel calls to application flushes when event population/order and enclosing intervals establish an unambiguous mapping. Never assume an offset or subtract clocks across client/server processes.
limits: A single heavily observed diagnostic does not demonstrate a mitigation or a new performance baseline.
Block events have no retained request pointer. Preserve independent issue/completion counts; do not invent a one-to-one pairing across partial completions or boundary events.
Additional kernel work inside an unexplained residual remains unattributed.
